title: Registers and counters
subtitle: Line up flip-flops and you can store a word, shift it, or count with it.

reg.title: Registers
reg.body: An n-bit register is n D flip-flops sharing one clock: on each clock edge all bits load in parallel. A load-enable input decides whether the register takes new data or holds. Registers are how a CPU keeps values between steps.
reg.steps: A 16-bit register has how many flip-flops? One per bit.

shift.title: Shift registers
shift.body: Connect each flip-flop’s Q to the next one’s D: on every clock edge the word shifts one place. Serial-in/serial-out delays data by n clocks; serial-in/parallel-out turns a bit stream into a word (and the reverse converts parallel to serial, used in UART/SPI). Shifting left multiplies by 2; right divides by 2.
shift.steps: 1011 shifted left by one (new bit 0). 0110 → value doubles, dropping the old top bit.

async.title: Asynchronous (ripple) counters
async.body: Chain T flip-flops (T = 1) so each one clocks the next: the first toggles every clock, the second every two, and so on — the outputs count in binary. An n-bit counter has 2ⁿ states and its top bit runs at f/2ⁿ. Drawback: the change ripples through, so outputs briefly show wrong values (glitches) and the max clock is limited by the delay of n stages.
async.steps: A 4-bit counter is clocked at 1600 Hz. Frequency of Q3 (the top bit): 1600 ÷ 2⁴.

sync.title: Synchronous counters
sync.body: In a synchronous counter every flip-flop shares the clock and logic decides which toggle: bit k toggles when all lower bits are 1. No ripple, so it is faster and glitch-free at the cost of a few AND gates. Up/down counting just changes that logic.

modn.title: Modulo-N counters
modn.body: To count 0…N−1, detect the state N and immediately reset (asynchronous clear) or load 0 (synchronous). A decade (mod-10) counter detects 1010 (10) and resets to 0000. Number of flip-flops needed: n = ⌈log₂ N⌉.
modn.steps: A mod-60 counter for seconds. Flip-flops needed: 2⁵ = 32 < 60 ≤ 64 = 2⁶, so six flip-flops.

ring.title: Ring and Johnson counters
ring.body: A ring counter circulates a single 1 round an n-bit shift register: n states, and each state is decoded by one bit (no logic). A Johnson (twisted-ring) counter feeds back the inverted last output, giving 2n states with the same flip-flops.
ring.steps: A 4-bit Johnson counter from 0000: 0000 → 1000 → 1100 → 1110 → 1111 → 0111 → 0011 → 0001 → 0000. That is 8 states from 4 flip-flops.
